content.title: Supervision for Therapists and Organizations
content.intro: Trauma therapy is complex, and therapists sometimes face a host of difficulties and dilemmas. In these situations, professional support and supervision are especially important; it is important not to deal with them alone. We offer therapists who work with trauma survivors individual supervision, group supervision in small groups, or supervision for intact teams in organizations.
challenges: How do you navigate between states of flooding and disconnection?
How do you deal with dissociative states?
Lack of cooperation and lack of engagement in therapy
Compassion fatigue and secondary traumatization of the therapist

options.title: Individual supervision
options.description: Individual supervision for therapists who work with trauma survivors.

options.title: Supervision for organizations

options.description: Supervision for intact teams in organizations, in a group of 3 to 5 therapists.

options.title: Supervision group
options.description: Trauma brings up feelings of isolation, difficulty telling one's story, and states of being stuck and helpless. In a parallel process, the trauma therapist experiences many of these same qualities in the work with trauma survivors. A supervision group makes it possible to draw on the experienced professional eye of a facilitator and of peers: to create movement where things are stuck, to bring language where there is misunderstanding, and to broaden the perspective beyond one's own professional experience and clinical sessions. A supervision group offers a deep look, sharing and resonance, peer support, encounters with a range of therapeutic stances, and professional and personal connections.
details: Group supervision in an intimate group of about 5 therapists
Six sessions of an hour and a quarter each
Once a week, on Zoom, starting May 14, 2025
suitableFor: Experienced therapists who are new to trauma therapy
notSuitableFor: Those who want supervision on complex trauma cases

options.title: Supervision group for Roadmap graduates
options.price: Additional fee; subject to the number of participants
options.description: After The Roadmap course, you can join a 5-session supervision group in which participants bring cases from their practice for consultation and work planning, and learn from other participants' cases.

options.title: Supervision in work with children (Metiv Children)
options.format: Individual or long-term support, in Jerusalem or on Zoom
options.description: Metiv Children offers professional supervision from psychologists and social workers who specialize in trauma. You can request focused supervision or long-term support.
